title: 5 charts: How crypto cards are driving stablecoin spend - a16z crypto
gist: Crypto payment card spend hit $759M/month in July, up 2.5x year-over-year, with settlement shifting from Gnosis/EURe concentration toward Optimism/Solana/Base and overwhelmingly dollar stablecoins (USDC, USDT) riding on Visa rails.

insights.claim: Monthly crypto payment card volume reached $759 million in July, up roughly 2.5x from $306 million a year earlier, and up from less than $1 million when Paymentscan tracking began in October 2023.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: Crypto card spend is compounding fast off a small base; investors should track Paymentscan's monthly volume series as a real-usage proxy for stablecoin adoption rather than relying on issuance/market-cap figures alone.
insights.quote: Monthly crypto payment card volume reached $759 million in July, up (roughly 2.5x) from $306 million a year earlier
insights.locator: Monthly crypto payment card volume reached $759 million

insights.claim: Nearly 9 million purchases were made using crypto payment cards in July, up from about 5.2 million a year earlier, implying an average transaction size of around $86.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: An ~$86 average ticket size signals everyday retail spend rather than large one-off transfers, suggesting crypto cards are being used as a genuine payments substitute, not just an offramp.
insights.quote: That puts the average amount spent per transaction at around $86.

insights.claim: For RedotPay, the largest crypto card program by volume, spending figures are self-reported by the issuer rather than independently observed onchain, unlike other tracked programs.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: The largest single data input to the headline growth figure is unverified issuer self-reporting, a data-quality caveat investors should weight when citing these totals.
insights.quote: For RedotPay, the largest program by volume, spending is self-reported by the issuer rather than observed onchain.

themes.theme: Settlement chain fragmentation away from Gnosis

insights.claim: Crypto card spending was concentrated on the Gnosis chain in early 2024 (home of Gnosis Pay, the first Visa card tied directly to a self-custodial wallet), but as of July, Optimism carries about 29% of volume, Solana about 19%, Base about 19%, and Gnosis has dropped to about 2%.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: Settlement-chain share is a fast-moving, contestable market as new card programs launch; L2s and Solana are capturing share from the early Gnosis incumbent, worth monitoring for which chain becomes the default payments rail.
insights.quote: As of July, Optimism carries about 29% of crypto card spend volume, Solana about 19%, and Base about 19%, according to Paymentscan. Gnosis has dropped to about 2%.
insights.locator: As of July, Optimism carries about 29%

insights.claim: Euro-backed stablecoin EURe dominated crypto card spend in early 2024 at around 88% of volume (mostly on Gnosis), but its share has fallen to about 2% as of July, while dollar-backed stablecoins now dominate: USDC handles about 58% of card spending (up from roughly 48% a year ago) and USDT about 26% (up from roughly 7%).
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: The shift from EURe to USDC/USDT tracks the broader chain migration away from Gnosis, reinforcing that dollar stablecoins are becoming the default settlement currency for crypto-linked consumer payments globally.
insights.quote: Crypto payment card spending now happens overwhelmingly in digital dollars.

themes.theme: Card network rails and market scale

insights.claim: Crypto payment cards remain a small market compared to traditional card networks, which process trillions of dollars per month, and among the tracked programs almost all transactions run through Visa rails.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: Stablecoin card growth is currently piggybacking on incumbent Visa infrastructure rather than displacing it, meaning near-term stablecoin payments upside accrues partly to existing card-network rails, not just crypto-native issuers.
insights.quote: For the tracked programs, this is happening almost entirely through Visa.
insights.locator: Crypto payment cards remain a small market

insights.claim: Crypto payment cards are described as one piece of a broader post-GENIUS crypto acceleration that also includes rapid adoption of stablecoins and tokenized assets.
insights.speaker: Robert Hackett
insights.so_what: a16z frames card spend growth as part of a post-GENIUS-Act regulatory tailwind for stablecoins broadly, suggesting investors should watch tokenized-asset adoption as a correlated trend, not an isolated card-payments story.
insights.locator: Crypto payment cards are one piece
